title: The crescent in the clay
subtitle: Po Dara's River Lotus has brought glazed storage jars from Champa. A granary porter swears the crescents on their shoulders mark them as jars that were taken from the royal yard.

evidence.label: 01  Manifest
evidence.title: The River Lotus’s declaration
evidence.text: Twelve glazed storage jars, empty and sound, for sale by the piece. Two smaller jars at the mast are the crew's drinking-water vessels and are marked as not for sale.

evidence.label: 02  At the display
evidence.title: A familiar shape
evidence.text: From the quay the crescents look the same. Up close, the twelve sale jars carry a narrow crescent pressed into the clay at the shoulder. Brown glaze runs unbroken down into each groove. One jar has a smear of red packing fibre caught at its lip.

evidence.label: 03  Testimony
evidence.title: Two descriptions of a crescent
evidence.text:
The granary porter: “The yard is missing jars. I saw that shape when ours went through the gate. From down here I'd swear to it.”

Po Dara: “The potter presses that crescent into every jar he makes. The steward's jars may be missing, but he won't find a trace of his paint on mine.”

evidence.label: 04  Compare marks
evidence.title: The yard's remaining jar
evidence.text: The storekeeper brings a jar from the missing set's row. Its crescent is red and brushed on top of smooth glaze. A damp rag lifts a little pigment at the end of the stroke. On the sale jars, there is no red in the grooves, on the glaze or on the rag. The stray fibre pulls away whole.

rulings.label: Major Fraud — hold the suspect cargo
Story Event — hold the ship and notify the court

reasons.label: The sale jars have fired-in grooves, not the granary's brushed crescent.
A matching crescent shape is enough to identify the granary's property.
The two jars at the mast are undeclared sale stock.
The red at one jar's lip is what remains of a porter's mark after someone tried to remove it.

feedback_by_method.measurements: The twelve jars match the count. That does not say whether they are the granary's jars.
feedback_by_method.testimony: The porter saw a shape from the quay and Po Dara offers another explanation. Compare a jar from each lot to settle it.
feedback_by_method.contents: The jars are empty as declared. What is inside cannot tell you which crescent was applied at the granary.
feedback_by_method.manifest: The declaration lists the jars for sale; it does not distinguish a fired groove from the granary's paint.

hidden_truth.success: In the temenggung’s name, you clear the River Lotus. The granary's crescent was laid over the glaze; these crescents went into the clay before firing. The porter touches the two shoulders in turn. “I can tell my steward which ones to look for now,” he says.
hidden_truth.clear: You clear the River Lotus, but leave the porter's accusation unanswered. Po Dara has to show the two marks to every buyer who heard him shout.
hidden_truth.unsupported: The evidence does not support amending the declaration in the temenggung’s name. A similar outline is not proof of common ownership.
hidden_truth.hold: You hold the River Lotus and call the court. Its men find a potter's mark, not the missing jars. Po Dara loses the day's market.

history_notes.note: Southeast Asian glazed jars circulated by sea as containers and trade wares; the exact Champa cargo is a plausible reconstruction (docs/research/commodities.md, §3.12; Orillaneda 2016).

Incised and stamped shoulder marks are attested on Santa Cruz jars, but their functions are unknown (docs/research/seals-marks-packaging.md, §2; Orillaneda, pp. 317–319). The two crescents, their meanings, the manifest and the dispute are gameplay inventions.
